# Meaning-bound specialization baseline

Four complete informed first projects and two explicit-binding repairs and two public-entry repairs are
preserved before implementation for Issue #44. Fourteen actual CLI checks bind
source, CLI and reused native-kernel bytes. Native invocation counts were not
instrumented. No source action or numerical oracle was executed.

Both initial finite positive definitions check, but initially lack an explicit
provider/Meaning bind. Their separately saved checked_op callers also check,
including the exact Unit minus scalar. The unchanged false X provider rejects
with a phase-fixed-meaning contract error in the finite route. The finite Nat
parameter example encounters its existing unsupported profile. Four first selected checks reject the Meaning-refined parameter before provider
checking. The two explicit-binding selected checks first fail because the new
entry is private. Their separately preserved public-entry repairs encounter the
unsupported checked_op constructor. Neither visibility nor profile refusals
validate the proposed semantic requirements.

The next implementation must retain exact type trees, phase, ordered axes,
owner/dependency identity, original declaration checking and native evidence.
It cannot ignore Meaning, infer it from a provider name or treat an ordinary
unitarity claim as equality. Nat/Basis specialization and operator access remain
separate. No new interpretation, guarantee, primitive meaning, static collection
or generic QFT delivery is proposed. These records do not close #44.
